ai.definition: A quantum internet refers to a network of interconnected nodes using quantum entanglement, enabling ultra-secure communications with unprecedented speed and privacy.
ai.howItWorks: Quantum repeaters and satellites are deployed to maintain signal integrity over long distances. Quantum entanglement is used to create secure communication channels between nodes, ensuring that any attempt at eavesdropping would disrupt the system.
ai.problemSolved: Current internet infrastructure lacks robust security measures against quantum computing attacks. A quantum internet provides a solution by offering unbreakable encryption and faster data transfer rates.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing and integrating quantum hardware such as qubits, quantum repeaters, and satellites with classical networking equipment.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing quantum circuits, fabricating qubits, testing repeaters for signal integrity, and integrating them into a network topology that can span continents or even the globe.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the complexity of quantum hardware, the need for specialized cooling systems, and the high energy requirements of quantum operations. Satellite deployment also adds significant expense.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising but faces significant technical challenges before widespread adoption can occur.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are in early stages of development, with no standardized regulations currently in place for quantum internet deployment and operation.
ai.risks: Technical risks include the fragility of qubits and the difficulty in maintaining long-distance signal integrity. Security risks involve potential vulnerabilities during the transition from classical to quantum networks.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to the current lack of widespread adoption and the high costs involved. Potential future markets could emerge in secure government communications, financial transactions, and sensitive data transfers.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving qubit stability, reducing energy consumption, and enhancing network scalability and reliability.

glossary.def: A phenomenon where quantum particles become interconnected such that the state of one particle can instantaneously affect the state of another, no matter the distance between them.
The basic unit of quantum information, analogous to a classical bit but capable of existing in multiple states simultaneously due to superposition.
Devices designed to maintain and amplify the entanglement between qubits over long distances, crucial for extending the reach of a quantum network.

subsystems.name: Quantum nodes
subsystems.role: store and process quantum information at each end of a link.
parts: quantum processors (trapped ions, neutral atoms, superconducting circuits)
quantum memories with long coherence times
interfaces between stationary qubits and photons

subsystems.name: Entangled photon sources
subsystems.role: create pairs of photons whose quantum states are linked.
parts: nonlinear crystals for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Transmission medium
subsystems.role: carry photons over hundreds to thousands of kilometres without losing their quantum state.
parts: satellites carrying entangled-photon sources or detectors

subsystems.name: Quantum repeaters
subsystems.role: extend entanglement beyond the range of direct fibre transmission by swapping and purifying entanglement at intermediate stations.

subsystems.name: Classical control plane
subsystems.role: synchronise clocks, route photons, and coordinate error correction across the network.
parts: precision timing (e.g. atomic clocks or GPS)

buildSteps.title: Fabricate quantum nodes
buildSteps.detail: Build trapped-ion, neutral-atom or superconducting qubit processors and pair them with quantum memories that can hold a state for milliseconds to seconds.

buildSteps.title: Generate entanglement
buildSteps.detail: Fire a laser through a nonlinear crystal to produce pairs of entangled photons, then separate them while preserving their quantum link.

buildSteps.title: Transmit photons
buildSteps.detail: Send one photon of each pair through optical fibre or a free-space telescope link to a distant node, using low-loss fibre or satellite passes.

buildSteps.title: Detect and verify entanglement
buildSteps.detail: Use single-photon detectors and precise timing to confirm that the two photons remain entangled after transmission.

buildSteps.title: Insert quantum repeaters
buildSteps.detail: At intermediate stations, store photons in quantum memories, perform Bell-state measurements to swap entanglement, and purify the result to extend range.

buildSteps.title: Run quantum key distribution
buildSteps.detail: As a first application, use the link to generate a secret key, either from entangled photons or from prepare-and-measure protocols, and test it against eavesdropping.

buildSteps.title: Integrate classical control
buildSteps.detail: Add classical channels and software to synchronise node clocks, route entanglement requests, and manage error correction across the network.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a multi-node network
buildSteps.detail: Connect many nodes into a mesh, then link distant regions via satellite to move toward a global quantum internet.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum memories with long coherence times
prerequisites.why: repeaters need to store entanglement long enough to synchronise with other nodes; laboratory demonstrations exist but are not yet practical at scale.
entanglement distribution demands near-perfect photons and detectors, and current systems still have too many losses and false counts for long chains.
no complete repeater has been built that can extend entanglement over hundreds of kilometres with the required fidelity and rate.
the Micius satellite demonstrated satellite quantum key distribution in 2016, but global entanglement distribution from orbit is not yet operational.
a scalable quantum network must correct errors without collapsing quantum states, and practical fault-tolerant protocols are still being researched.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point quantum key distribution over fibre (up to a few hundred kilometres) and trusted-node networks spanning thousands of kilometres, for example in China and Europe
pathway.unlocks: secure communication for governments and financial institutions, but only with trusted relay stations.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters that extend entanglement over 500 km or more without trusted nodes
pathway.unlocks: long-distance secure links that rely on physics rather than trust in intermediate stations.

pathway.milestone: multi-node entanglement networks linking quantum processors in different cities
pathway.unlocks: distributed quantum computing and enhanced quantum sensing across a network.

pathway.milestone: satellite-based entanglement distribution and interoperable global standards
pathway.unlocks: a true quantum internet connecting devices worldwide with unbreakable security and shared quantum processing.
